###Part A — Creating Vectors and List:

```{r}
#Question #1:

#A factory has a census of its workers. There are 50 workers in total. The following list shows their ages: `34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24,33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18.

#Create a vector for the worker’s age.

ages <- c(
  34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 
  35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 
  50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 
  35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 
  48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18
)
ages

```
How many data points?
50 data points

Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.
Minimum age: 17

Maximum age: 61


```{r}
#Access the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.

ages[13:18] 
elements_33_to_35 <- ages[33:35] 

```
```{r}
filtered_ages <- ages[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]
filtered_ages
```
```{r}
ages[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
ages
```

```{r}


#Question #2:

#R has actually lots of built-in datasets.
#For example, the rivers data “gives the lengths (in miles) of 141 “major” rivers in North America, as compiled by the US Geological Survey”.
#Use data(rivers)
#Get the number of elements (length) in rivers, their sum (sum), mean (mean), median(median), variance(var), standard deviation(sd), minimum (min) and maximum (max).


# Compute statistics and store them in a single vector
river_stats <- c(
  length = length(rivers),
  sum    = sum(rivers),
  mean   = mean(rivers),
  median = median(rivers),
  var    = var(rivers),
  sd     = sd(rivers),
  min    = min(rivers),
  max    = max(rivers)
)

river_stats
```



What is the result? The derived result must be in just one(1) vector name.
 length         sum        mean      median         var          sd         min         max 
   141.0000  83357.0000    591.1844    425.0000 243908.4086    493.8708    135.0000   3710.0000 
   
   
```{r}
#Question #3:

#The table below gives the 25 most powerful celebrities and their annual pay as ranked by the editions of Forbes magazine and as listed on the Forbes.com website.
# 1. Vector of Celebrity Names
celebrity <- c(
  "Lady Gaga", "Oprah Winfrey", "Justin Bieber", "U2", "Elton John",
  "Tiger Woods", "Taylor Swift", "Bon Jovi", "Simon Cowell", "LeBron James",
  "Angelina Jolie", "Katy Perry", "Johnny Depp", "Kobe Bryant", "Leonardo DiCaprio",
  "Black Eyed Peas", "Donald Trump", "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Tyler Perry", "Paul McCartney",
  "Kim Kardashian", "George Lucas", "Simon Fuller", "Kanye West", "Usher"
)


rank <- 1:25


pay <- c(
  90, 290, 53, 195, 100,
  75, 45, 125, 90, 48,
  30, 44, 50, 53, 77,
  61, 60, 80, 130, 67,
  12, 50, 80, 16, 46
)
celebrity
rank
pay


```
```{r}
#Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling. Change power ranking to 15 and pay to 90.

# Initial vectors
celebrity <- c(
  "Lady Gaga", "Oprah Winfrey", "Justin Bieber", "U2", "Elton John",
  "Tiger Woods", "Taylor Swift", "Bon Jovi", "Simon Cowell", "LeBron James",
  "Angelina Jolie", "Katy Perry", "Johnny Depp", "Kobe Bryant", "Leonardo DiCaprio",
  "Black Eyed Peas", "Donald Trump", "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Tyler Perry", "Paul McCartney",
  "Kim Kardashian", "George Lucas", "Simon Fuller", "Kanye West", "Usher"
)

rank <- 1:25

pay <- c(
  90, 290, 53, 195, 100,
  75, 45, 125, 90, 48,
  30, 44, 50, 53, 77,
  61, 60, 80, 130, 67,
  12, 50, 80, 16, 46
)

# Modify 15th position (Power Ranking = 15, Pay = 90)
celebrity[15] <- "J.K. Rowling"
pay[15] <- 90

# Print updated vectors
print(celebrity)
print(rank)
print(pay)
```
```{r}
#Question #4:

#Create a list of ten (10) vegetables you ate during your lifetime. If none, just list down the vegetables in your mind.

vegetables <- c("Carrots", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Tomatoes", "Potatoes", "Cucumbers", "Onions", "Garlic",  "PeppeBellrs", "Cabbage")
vegetables



#Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list. What is the result?

vegetables <- c(vegetables, "Eggplant", "Zucchini")
vegetables

#How many datapoints do you have?
length(vegetables)
# Output: [1] 12
```
```{r}
#Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
vegetables <- c(
  "Carrots", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Tomatoes", "Potatoes",
  "Cucumbers", "Onions", "Garlic", "Bell Peppers", "Cabbage",
  "Eggplant", "Zucchini"
)


vegetables <- append(vegetables, c("Cauliflower", "Kale", "Asparagus", "Peas"), after = 5)
vegetables



#How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
length(vegetables)
# Output: [1] 16
```
